 ......
 JUDGMENT The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 01.04.2021.
2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 01.04.2021 at about 01.10pm the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-JP-6444 on Kanakapura Road, when he reached in front of South Thindies SCCH - 25 3 MVC No. 2152/2021 Hotel, Basavanagudi, a Car bearing No.KA-02-ML-4133 which was proceeding in right side of the petitioner suddenly came to extreme left side without giving any indication or signal in a rash and negligent manner by violating the traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle, due to impact petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. 
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Deepak Hospital, wherein admitted and treated as an inpatient, surgery was done and discharged on 05.04.2021 with an advice of non weight bearing, to be under regular physiotherapy and followup treatment and complete bed rest. So far he has spent Rs.1,25,000/- towards medical expenses,
conveyance, food and nourishment etc., At the time of accident he was hale and healthy, working as a Team Leader at M/s Prerana Motors Pvt. Ltd., Bangalore and earning a sum of Rs.26,500/- per month and also monthly incentives around Rs.10,000/- per month. Due to accidental injuries the petitioner is bound to bed and could not do his work. He is put SCCH - 25 4 MVC No. 2152/2021 to great hardship and mental agony and shock. The accident caused due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-ML-4133. The jurisdictional Basavanagudi Traffic police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.0011/2021 p/u/Sec.279 & 337 of IPC. Therefore, the 1 st respondent being the RC Owner and the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him. Hence, this petition. 
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements. 
5. The objection of the respondent No.1. 
He has denied the petitioner averments, He has averred that the vehicle is insured with the Sharath.S vs Muniraju.G on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188041651/
2 respondent No.2 and has valid insurance policy. He has denied the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car. The driver of the car had a SCCH - 25 5 MVC No. 2152/2021 valid DL as on the date of accident. Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition. 
6. The objection of the respondent No.2. 
It has denied the petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the 1 st respondent in respect of the Car bearing No.KA-02-ML-4133. There is non-compliance of Sec.134(c)
and 158(6) of MV Act. The driver of the offending Car did not have valid DL as on the date of accident. Further denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the Car in the accident. 
The petitioner was not wearing ISI marked headguard at the time of accident. The petitioner was not holding valid DL to ride the vehicle as on the date of accident. There was a negligence on the part of the petitioner as on the date of accident. It has also denied the age, occupation and the manner of accident. It has contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive,
arbitrary and disproportionate. Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it. 
SCCH - 25 6 MVC No. 2152/2021 7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-ML-4113 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries? 
2. Whether the Petitioner he is entitled for Compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award? 
8. The Petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.17. Mr. Sathish Rao - Incharge Medical Records Department at Deepak Hospital, got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.18 to 20. Dr. Nagaraj B.N. examined as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.21 to 22. On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf. 
9. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
SCCH - 25 7 MVC No. 2152/2021 10. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
Sharath.S vs Muniraju.G on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188041651/
3  for the following:-
 REASONS  11. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-ML-4113, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.8. He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination. During his cross examination he has stated that due to his treatment and since his parents were unable to understand the consequences they gave the complaint after Two days of the accident. There was a cement wall dividing the road in the center. At the time of accident his bike was very near to the divider and the said road is a heavy traffic area. He has also got examined the MRO of Deepak Hospital, Bangalore, as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.18 to P.20 SCCH - 25 8 MVC No. 2152/2021 i.e., Authorization letter, MLC register extract and case sheet. During his cross examination nothing worthwhile is elicited. The Respondent No.2 insurer has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle and manner of accident. In order to prove its contention it has not examined any witness. 
12. As per FIR, it was registered after 3 days of the accident on the complaint of the petitioner himself at Ex . P.1. Ex.P.2 is the Medico Legal Register shows the details of the accident dated 01.04.2021 and time of the arrival of the patient as 1.20pm along with injuries suffered by the petitioner and this information was given to the police on 02.04.2021 at 19.45pm. Exs. P.3 & 4 spot mahazar and spot sketch shows, the manner of accident and the spot where the accident occurred. 
Ex.P.5 is the statements of an eyewitness which support the case of the petitioner. MV Accident Report at Ex . P.6 shows the damages of the petitioner's motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JP-6444 to the front headlight mask, left side front indicator, front number plate, left side safety bumper scratch guard and left side front steering handle bar SCCH - 25 9 MVC No. 2152/2021 shield of the motorcycle damaged. In the same manner the offending Car bearing No.KA-02-ML-4133 damaged to its front right side door and fender of the motor vehicle. Except the above said damages of both the motor vehicles rest of all the parts were in order. Ex . P.7 notice given to the RC owner of the Car and reply. The police have conducted investigation and filed the charge sheet as per Ex.P.8 against the driver of the Car. Ex.P.9 is the order sheet in CC No.2338/2021 and Ex.P.10 Wound Certificate shows that the petitioner was hit by the Car and has suffered injuries in RTA which occurred on 01.04.2021. The sketch at Ex.P.4 shows that the offending Car has suddenly taken right. All these documents show that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-ML-4113. Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative. 
13. Issue Nos.2 & 3:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.10. As per Ex.P.10 the Petitioner has SCCH - 25 10 MVC No. 2152/2021 sustained Right Bimallular Fracture which is grievous in nature. 
Sharath.S vs Muniraju. G on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188041651/
4 14. The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.21 & 22 clinical notes and X-ray He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed with right ankle Bimalleolar fracture, treated at Deepak Hospital with ORIF with plate and Screws. He further stated that the petitioner is suffering from physical disability of the right lower limbs at 41% and to the whole body physical disability at 14%.
15. PW.2 in his cross examination has stated that, he has not treated the petitioner. The injuries are 4 years old as on the date of assessment. The fractures are united and implants are in situ. There is minimal restriction. 
Disability:
16. From the evidence of PW.2 and the documents on record, it is clear that the petitioner has suffered Bimalleolar SCCH - 25 11 MVC No. 2152/2021 fracture. So it will be difficult for him to Walk. He has stated that he was doing Team Leader Work. This means that he has to walk and do the work. This kind of disability will affect his day to day work. As per the say of the PW.2 the fracture are 4 years old. Considering the age of the petitioner and the fracture, this court deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 10%. 
Monthly income:
17. The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working as a Team Leader at M/s Prerana Motors Pvt. Ltd., and earning Rs.26,500/- per month and also getting monthly incentives around Rs.10,000/- per month. In this regard he has produced Salary slip and Service Certificate at Exs.P.14 & 15. As per Pay Slip of March 2021 his total salary was Rs.26,513/-. As per service letter it shows that at the time of accident he was working at Prerana Motors (p) Ltd. Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the income of the petitioner at Rs.26,513/- per month. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 31 years as could be made out SCCH - 25 12 MVC No. 2152/2021 from Exs.P.16 & 17/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card and DL. He was hale and healthy before the accident. 
Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:- 
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Deepak Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 01.04.2021 to 05.04.2021 and was diagnosed with Right Bimalleolar Fracture and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.11. Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone are grievous in nature. Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.70,000/- under this head. 
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES: 
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc. In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.12 for a sum SCCH - 25 13 MVC No. 2152/2021 of Rs.1,69,706/-
Sharath. S vs Muniraju.G on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188041651/
5 which includes Ambulance bills of Rs.7,500/-, it has to be deducted then the balance comes to Rs.1,62,206/-. There is no contrary evidence against these bills from the Respondents. Therefore,
the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head. 
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries. The petitioner has produced discharge summary of Deepak Hospital at Ex.P.11 to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital and also produced a letter from Prerana Motors (P)
Ltd., as per Ex.P.13. As per Ex.P.13 it is mentioned that due to the Road Accident, the petitioner has sustained Major leg injury and availed leave (leave without pay) from 1st April 2021 to 30.06.2021, total Three months leave. Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Three month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him and the the payment of that particular period has to SCCH - 25 14 MVC No. 2152/2021 reimbursed. Hence,
he is entitled for a sum of Rs.79,539/-
under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
As per letter at Ex.P.15 the petitioner has continued to work in the same organization till 31.08.2023. The date of accident is 01.04.2021. This shows that he has continued in his work and has not suffered any financial loss or Loss of Income in the aftermath of the accident. Therefore, he is not entitled to get any compensation under this head. 
 (v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:- 
The Petitioner was aged about 31 years at the time of accident. He has sustained simple and grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 10% functional disability. The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life. Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts. Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head. 
 SCCH - 25 15 MVC No. 2152/2021  (vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND  NOURISHMENT CHARGES: 
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise. However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses. In this regard he has produced Ambulance Bills at Ex.P.12 for Rs.7,500/-. He is entitled for the said amount for transportation. 
Sharath.S vs Muniraju. G on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188041651/
6 Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head. 
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of PW.3, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implants and the estimation of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-. In this regard neither the petitioner nor PW.3 has produced any estimation bill about further surgery. As per the evidence of Pws.1 & 3 and looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an SCCH - 25 16 MVC No. 2152/2021 amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded to the Petitioner under this head. Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head. 
18. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.70,000/-
2. Medical expenses s.1,62,206/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.79,539/- period 4. Loss of future income NIL 5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/- nourishment charges 7. Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/-
TOTAL Rs.3,71,745/-
If it is rounded off it comes to around Rs.3,72,000/- and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner. 
Liability 19. The Respondents have contended that the driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA-02-ML-4113 did not have a SCCH - 25 17 MVC No. 2152/2021 valid and effective DL and also the petitioner did not have valid DL to ride the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JP-6444 as on the date of accident. However, they have not proved their defence as discussed above. Therefore, the Respondents being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner. However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner. The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.25,00,000/-
Sharath.S vs Muniraju.G on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188041651/
7 but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.3,72,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed. Accordingly, Issue No.3 is held in the affirmative. 
20. Issue No.4:-
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass SCCH - 25 18 MVC No. 2152/2021 the following:-
ORDER The petition is allowed in part with cost. The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,72,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Seventy Two Thousand only)
along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount. The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner. 
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award. 
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules. 
SCCH - 25 19 MVC No. 2152/2021 Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-. Draw decree accordingly.
